absent: Exact page order computation and frozen page allocator failure modes beyond node selection.
Per processor sheaf layout, capacity policy, locking, and flush mechanics.
Slab slow paths, partial list management, and remote node defragmentation behavior.
Sanitizer, leak detector, profiling, failure injection, and usercopy enforcement semantics.
Presentation layer cache representation beyond unlink, alias, and release.
Full bucket size table, index mapping, and early cache initialization sequence.
RCU sheaf flushing and general RCU barrier interaction details.
Alignment, padding, and reciprocal sizing arithmetic.

findings.text: Cache creation provides a global constructor that reuses a compatible existing cache when merging allows it and otherwise builds a new cache, performing validation, flag filtering, alignment preparation, locking, and error reporting, failing to null with optional panic on request.

Bucket family creation provides isolated per size caches for a named owner with usercopy window and constructor, returning a sentinel when the feature is disabled and null on early use or allocation failure, rolling back partially created members on error.

Cache destruction safely ignores null input, drains in flight deferred and RCU work, decrements the reference count under protection, returns early for remaining aliases, otherwise checks for live objects, unlinks from the global list, releases presentation state, and completes teardown when empty.
Release handling selects between presentation backed teardown and direct teardown based on build support and lifecycle stage, then disposes of the duplicated name and the backing control object.
Barrier services synchronize per processor deferred work and RCU activity before teardown, with one variant additionally flushing sheaf state when that facility exists for the cache.

Large allocation accepts a byte size, caller flags, and a node selector, derives a page order, normalizes disallowed flags, requires compound pages, chooses between generic and node specific frozen page sources, and on success establishes addressability with reclaim accounting and large marking before running sanitizer and leak hooks in tag aware order.

Nolock allocation offers a nonblocking trylock only path that validates context, enforces nonwarning nonreclaiming behavior, normalizes node policy, distinguishes zero size and oversize outcomes, requires wide atomic support unless debugging, prefers a per processor fast path then a direct slab path without incompatible hooks, allows at most one retry into the next larger size, and completes with pointer sanitization plus post hooks.

Freelist state combines a head pointer with packed counters for in use and total objects plus a frozen indicator that doubles as corruption indication under debugging, with additional extension flags on wide builds and an optional combined full width view for atomic protection against reuse hazards.

Slab control overlays page control with ownership and linkage state, offering two exclusive views for active management versus deferred reclamation, alongside type and reference state and an optional extension base, with enforced offset equivalence to the page view for shared fields.

Cache control aggregates per processor sheaf state, full versus user visible sizing, sizing reciprocal, free pointer placement, sheaf capacity, growth policy, allocation policy, reference count, construction callback, metadata offsets, alignment, padding, display name, global linkage, and conditional presentation, hardening, placement, randomization, sanitizer, usercopy, statistics, and per node state.
Usage snapshot aggregates active versus total objects and slabs together with shared availability and sizing hints for limit, batch, shared, per slab density, and order.
Per object extension is an aligned pointer sized union carrying optional membership and profiling references only when those facilities are enabled.
Debug introspection captures the queried pointer, containing slab, object base, data offset, owning cache, return site, and bounded allocation and free call stacks.
Family description pairs per type display names with bucket sizes, while companion descriptors encode order policy and per node barn plus node control pairing.

Lifecycle advances from down with no service to partial with node structures ready to up with caches usable without extras to full with all services ready, tracked by a global stage variable that gates presentation linkage and teardown choices.
Freelist atomic update width adapts to platform capability, using a double width form with a wide combined type where available and a single width form with a narrow combined type otherwise.

Merging is suppressed by a global boot default, unmergeable creation arguments, forbidden flag membership, explicit capacity requests, and per cache opt out; reuse requires matching reclaim and placement and accounting behavior, compatible alignment, and close sizing without excessive waste, scanning existing caches in reverse to favor the smallest fit and widening user visible extents on alias reuse with a reference increment.

Creation validates name presence, execution context, and size bounds, filters unsupported flags, enables debug infrastructure on demand, forces isolation for explicit sheaf capacity, defaults to account capability unless disabled, sanitizes the usercopy window, warns on duplicate or space containing names without failing, and strictly checks custom free pointer requests for bounds, alignment, and safe reclamation support.

Object location derives the containing object start from an interior pointer by distinguishing virtual versus slab versus special allocator provenance, adjusting for padding and sanitizer tags, deriving indices from slab base and object stride, and clamping rounded addresses to the final object in the slab.
Large allocation sizing is recovered from the low byte of the companion page flags as an order value, with byte extent obtained by scaling the base page size by that order.

In the routed configuration, allocation tracking display, unit test detection, debug presentation release, and system presentation unlink and alias and release collapse to inert operations with neutral results.
Flag interrogation threads an implicit allocation token through a wrapper, common path tracing is enabled by a creation marker, and the bucket metadata cache pointer is fixed after initialization.

Global cache mutex serializes creation, alias search, reference changes, list linkage, and shutdown inspection, while processor set read protection spans destruction decisions and sheaf flushing, with deferred and RCU barriers completed before lock acquisition and release in reverse order of acquisition.

Nolock context never blocks and never takes sleeping locks, proceeding only when trylock primitives are usable and abandoning on contention, avoiding preallocation hooks and failure injection paths that are incompatible with trylock mode.

Teardown with remaining objects warns outside unit tests yet still unlinks, aliased references avoid teardown via early return, partial bucket family construction requires rollback of created members, and confusing names risk misleading external tools without failing creation.

Use of spinning permission or disallowed reclaim flags in nolock context indicates misuse, platforms lacking wide atomic support cannot use the fast path outside debugging, frozen state is ambiguous with corruption under debugging, and debug hook order must respect address tagging to preserve leak tracking.
Flag groupings separate persistent core behavior from diagnostic options from the accepted set and separately define the set that forbids merging and the subset that must match for reuse.
Presentation integration is declared available, per stack debug capture depth is sixteen entries, and lifecycle stages follow down then partial then up then full in increasing readiness.
